correctness.rationale: PASS. Dihedral and layer-swap averaging of arbitrary symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal stochastic P on C_n□K2 reduces the optimum value to rim q and rung p=1-2q with q∈[0,1/2]. The exact Fourier branches θ_k+=1-qλ_k and θ_k-=-1+q(4-λ_k), λ_k=2-2cos(2πk/n), include all 2n modes. Every even prism is bipartite, so s with Ps=-s gives SLEM=1 for every admissible P. For odd n, ε=2-2cos(π/n), the necessary lower bound max(|4q-1|,1-q ε) is uniquely minimized at q=2/(4+ε), p=ε/(4+ε), μ=(4-ε)/(4+ε); inequalities ε≤δ,Λ≤4 bound all remaining symmetric/antisymmetric Fourier modes and prove attainment. The odd gap is π²/(2n²)+O(n^-4), one-quarter of the holding-permitted leading gap. Boundary n=3 is a triangular prism with distinct rim and rung edges; n even includes degenerate/disconnected walks.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. Standard spectral FMMC symmetrization and Cartesian-product eigenvalues are established by Boyd and collaborators, and a related cyclic-prism problem allowing holding admits a different optimizer. Imposing zero diagonal is not a substitution in that solution: it forces period two for even n and a distinct two-mode balancing condition for odd n. The inspected primary work did not give the complete loopless all-n optimum; specialization under another name remains possible.
residual_risks: Could be a classical loopless random walk extremum under periodic graph/SLEM nomenclature outside retrieved literature.
